nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. If $F$ is continuous at a point $x \in \mathbb{R}$, then the boundary of the half-line $(-\infty, x]$, which is $\{x\}$, has $\mu$-measure zero.
nodes.title: Continuity points of the cdf have null boundary

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. If $F$ is continuous at a point $x \in \mathbb{R}$, then $\mu(\{x\}) = 0$.
nodes.title: No atom at a continuity point of the cdf

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. For every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $F$ is continuous at $x$ if and only if $\mu(\{x\}) = 0$.
nodes.title: The cdf is continuous exactly at the non-atoms

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. The set of points $x \in \mathbb{R}$ at which $F$ is continuous is dense in $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The continuity points of the cdf are dense

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, the measure $\mu((a, b])$ equals $\max(F(b) - F(a), 0)$, as an extended nonnegative real.
nodes.title: Mass of a half-open interval via the cdf

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$, and for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ let $F(x^-) = \lim_{y \to x^-} F(y)$ be its left limit at $x$. Then $\mu(\{x\})$ equals the jump $F(x) - F(x^-)$, which is a nonnegative real number since $F$ is nondecreasing.
nodes.title: Atoms are the jumps of the cdf

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
